What you're saying really helps me. I've been sort of floating since high school and while I'm doing reasonably well for myself in the IT world, I really want to get an Aquaponics business off the ground. Do you have any suggestions insofar as things I could be reading about hydroponics, or modern urban farming practices in general? Also, have you considered developing a vermiculture process to harvest the resulting fertilizer?

I've started dabbling in aquaponics. It certainly has some potential insofar as reducing waste and inefficiencies. However, should one wish to kick start a business, the Department of Fisheries and Oceans is less than forgiving when seeking special varieties of fish (being ones which compliment the nutritional needs of particular plants.) For the most part, Talapia fish are the most pH flexible (they have quite a range where they can survive) but their excrement leaves to be desired for fruting plants (i.e. tomatoes, peppers, cucumber, squash etc.) As well, their preference for light usually limits one to T5 types (rather than HPS, MH or LED) due to spectrum and heat. This could only be counteracted by an oversized reservoir or huge growing space with heat regulation. I'm still experimenting, but so far, aeroponics (being a subtype of hydro) is the most efficient that I'm aware of.

For literature, online forums and youtube are great. Even marijuana based grow guides help as far as systems and nutrients go. The best way to become proficient is simply to dive in! You can easily create a simple setup for under 100$. There are also tonnes of food security groups in the province which have many gardening/farming and hydro enthusiasts participating which will gladly share knowledge or even mentor. As long as you can put up with general hippieness and a mild PC enviroment, they're great! Lots of hugs and feelings, but lots of knowledge too.

Lastly, if ever you visit Moncton in the near future, pay Dieppe Hydroponics a visit or if you can handle the crazy, Atlantic Hydroponics Supply. Both establishments have some very knowledgeable staff than can get you pointed in the right direction.

Whatever you do, keep with the IT. If there's one frontier for food growing and security, robotics and automation will play a HUGE role.
